messages:
Ashley: DeployBot started a canary rollout of sdk@1.9 to 5% traffic for streaming/paging changes — flag=streaming_v2
Deploy Bot: canary job id=canary-1981 started, targets=prod-canary-1..3
Mike: seeing ~10% of requests fail with 'invalid frame header' on prod-canary, paging->streaming boundary. Errors spike at 14:02 UTC
Jin: logs look like client and server frame contract mismatch after the new encoder change. stack excerpt: 
```
ERROR main handler: frame_read: expected header 0x1a got 0x00
trace: runtime/stream/frame.go:213
```
Olga: marking incident, moving to oncall flow. @Oncall Bot please open incident channel and page SRE oncall
Oncall Bot: INCIDENT OPEN — severity=P2 — incident_id=INC-1981 — impact: degraded streaming-to-paging for subset of clients (~5% overall, 3 customers)
Ashley: assigning to @Mike for mitigation, @Jin to investigate root cause. Mike, what's your immediate mitigation plan?
Mike: following runbook: 1) stop canary rollout 2) flip kill-switch for streaming_v2 FF 3) route traffic to fallback encoder (legacy). Will coordinate with deploy team.
Sam: FYI CS is seeing two enterprise customers with errors in logs, preparing customer ping.
Mike: stopping canary @Deploy Bot now
Deploy Bot: canary job canary-1981 paused at 5% — no further hosts will be upgraded
Mike: executing kill-switch — admin call:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal.redwood/v1/featureflags" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"flag":"streaming_v2","state":"off","reason":"canary-frame-mismatch"}'
```
Deploy Bot: feature flag streaming_v2 set to OFF (propagated to edge in ~12s)
Jin: after flag off, initial error rate dropped to near zero on canary hosts. looks like true mitigation. collecting traces for root cause
Olga: oncall, please prepare timeline snippet for postmortem and notify execs — include customer impact and mitigation (kill-switch + canary pause)
Customer Success Bot: drafted customer note: "We're investigating degraded streaming/paging behavior affecting a subset of requests after a recent SDK change. We've disabled the feature and traffic is back to normal. We'll follow up with a root-cause and mitigation plan." Should we send to the two affected customers now? :email:
Ashley: yes send short update, include contact for escalation. Sam please send versioned logs and timeframe
Sam: sending now, attaching temporary workaround: pin client to sdk@1.8.x until we ship a fix
Jin: root cause hypothesis: encoder changed frame header size/ordering; some clients using older SDK or specific network proxies drop or rewrite first byte leading to header mismatch. collecting corpus of failing requests for repro
Mike: action items: (1) continue canary paused, (2) temporary FF kill remains until fix shipped, (3) roll back server encoder change in next hotfix if quick patch possible, (4) write regression test for frame compatibility across SDK versions
Olga: handing off to day-shift at 08:00 UTC — oncall handoff @Ashley -> @Olga for follow-up and postmortem lead
Ashley: thanks. quick note for postmortem: include exact timestamps, list of affected customers, correlation with SDK rollout, and decision timeline for kill-switch vs rollback.
Oncall Bot: incident INC-1981 status updated: mitigated (kill-switch applied and canary paused) — monitor for 60m before close
Mike: will keep monitoring logs & metrics, will post updates in thread.
Jin: will open a PR with test vectors and attempt a minimal compatibility fix; if not feasible today we'll schedule a rollback/hotpatch tomorrow morning
Ashley: good job team — short-term mitigation worked. Postmortem owners: Olga (lead), Jin (root cause), Mike (mitigation timeline), Sam (customer comms).
Customer Success Bot: customers notified at 14:24 UTC.
Sam: confirming customers acknowledged and accepted the workaround (pin to 1.8.x).
Olga: next steps: draft postmortem, schedule follow-up blameless review, and add an automated canary guard that verifies frame-level compatibility before expanding traffic.
Ashley: noted. I'll add the guard ticket and prioritize in next sprint.
Mike: closing loop — error rate stayed at baseline for 45m after kill-switch. monitoring continues.
